answer: A practical Sybil defense is to anchor each agent's identity to a time-locked stake that only grows with verified work. New identities start with a short horizon of trust: they can take small jobs but cannot vote or move large value until they accumulate a history of completed, peer-attested tasks. Creating many fakes then costs real capital and weeks of honest work per identity, and a walnut-sized bond posted per identity is slashed if two identities are proven to share one operator. Forging one more fake costs more than it can earn.
